nodes.text: xii. sins of our fathers
I look good. I smell good. I flash big carnivore grin, half my hair slicked back, sports jacket over Freddy Kreuger sweatshirt, half my hair a tangle of mad scientist effluvium.
I strut onto the floor, body already finding sine wave to move to. I look to my left and find fire and to my right, the stars. The girls on my arms grip tight to feel my body tighten in response.

I pull them with me, they find momentum and sling-shot out there, spinning and twirling, touching arms and back and butt and breast. They collide in the middle, a liquid pour of heat into an already visible fog bank.

Martin Link fell in love with a Kathleen Frenger. I can only imagine what that must have been like, as it was never a conversation we got to have. She rejected him for two years, she in love with somebody else.
His persistence paid off with an unintended me. There was much conflict in this union.

My heart is being destroyed by a randomeight. I explain to her that I will write about her and she explains she knew this going in. Why are we still holding back cards, to make it interesting, I think.
She flashes her tail at me, her eyes meeting mine her head peeking back behind.

It is some years later, she is married and I can't stop thinking about her. The dream of her is just as tangible and I do nothing if not live by my dreams. There are plenty of good reasons to stay away from her and plenty of reasons not to.
I avoid her out of a sense of respect for her reality. I don't want to undo so much hard work. I know I am capable of this and that scares me.

It is not a sense of now or then, just the possibility of us, never receding. I am shark prowling through cold dark waters senses all tuned to that one pursuit. I am telling her about my five year plan.
It goes ahead without her active involvement.
Or does it.
I show teeth to win them to me. I am warm and happy but I am aware and dangerous with that knowledge. I only want the best for them, long as it runs counterwise to my own self-interest.

I have heart and getting that broke only makes me eager to share in that bladed knowledge. The cycle of pain we unleash upon our lovers. Are we good enough, are they good enough, where do we measure up against all the rest.
What is this game we play and why are the rules always changing. I love how everyone tries so hard to ignore this.
The inability to express the horrible gravity of the situation. To tell her of all the untold destruction she'll cause in years to come. How she only makes it worse on herself.
I try to tell her not as threat but as a warning. That sort of anguish I do not wish on the one I love but that is the rotten truth of the matter. It's not an easy game we play, life or death.

Try not to show all your cards at once, try to keep things interesting. Know that true love should not only love you, true love should fear you, true love should frequently call both your sanities into question, true love should destroy you entirely then rebuild according to code.

Sad when we fail to see just how flawed the whole thing is really, just a shell game of time, place and circumstance. The stories we tell ourselves before during and after the fact just have to suffice. I forget none of her truths and none of her lies, until that is, they forget me.

Who was she protecting exactly. True love is also a dominant fiction made truth by the selfish desires of humanity, yet it compels me no less. If anything, recognition for everything it is and is not, gives me further strength and resolve to live this life by those impossible standards.
I rummage through my bedroom for a book, drunk and stupid. I stop looking, Smith turns and asks what is it. I shrug and say, I just know the girl I'm going to marry.
Who is it he asks, I keep looking for the book. It's so stupid, here it is.
We are married, why we do this, I don't know. Because it's a moment we fight for, tooth and nail. Children are coming, beautiful children.
Will we be happy, we as a construct. Not an individual happiness, but a swirling pool of male and female and other. She touches my head and holds my eye.

Her voice is one of the few I find peace with. Her voice is really nothing but the intent of her intellect carried by vibration through air, a music I appreciate on my own terms. I know the timber, the pitch and intonation.
She doesn't have to say much anymore for me to know everything. She is afraid peace will pacify me. Nothing will pacify me, not even death.
I burn so bright by her light. I live to live and will fight for any moments we can share together just the two of us. I know each moment is special.
My parents lived much of their lives apart. As a child, I could feel the lingering sense of anticipation, a growing bond of trust and determination. They were separate but never separated.
All I know is that my mother loved my father far more when I was twelve than when I was five.

I am single and will remain single for a very long time. It has ceased to be a test of willpower and has instead become a wholly rewarding lifestyle. I love women, have and will continue to love women.

But the woman eludes me. For the time being, I am insane enough without a gal in my life. I work and plot and scheme and since they love to spoil by their playful nature, I can't help but keep a healthy distance.

I love them for the games we choose to play together, I love to hear about the games they play when I am not around. The ugly truths they reveal in confidence are like the dead things a cat leaves at your feet. They smile watching our singular reaction and never reveal if we pass their test.

We seek our angels and demons, we want our perfect opposite to be a complimentary mix of those two spheres. Angelic in beauty, devotion, art and truth. Demonic in the flesh, twisting in our skins, gnawing our desires, lying to our hearts, birthing something just as mortal and flawed as we are.
To give birth to death, to know even your unborn child will suffer and die. It will be glorious.

I look for the good and bad. There are good traits I find offensive and bad I find seductive. I am human being ergo biological shorthand trigger beast, sensualist, social mores dug in very deep, personal touches provided by my own pater familiar martin link.

He smiles whenever I frown, he accepts my loss because he is a dead man. I can only assume his prerogative, thankee kindly, I kill with my heart and mind. Water faucet drip a constant winnow against rising tide.
What leaks breaks forth upon the dawning. What contains a loss. The vessels that preserve ballast against cold hard sink break upon crush.
Pressure tided up against the retaining metal wall of human uncertainty.
I watch my father die and his voice flows into me. I am the only one watching but I am not the only one receiving. With time the enormity really hits me.
It was just not Martin Link's voice showing me the way, it was all my fathers' voices.

The earth man who lived and walked and played upon his earth, every cell and animal whose singular survival shaped the path I find myself on, yet he is the father that remains special as it was his voice and life that taught me the way, it is his voice I still hear in my head.

A kind and rational man who fought his own battles on his own terms and kept his honor and composure through trial and error. He was my globe-trotting academic athlete sci-fi super-hero. He is earth man.
